title: Robert F. Kennedy in the 1968 Record
metaDescription: Robert F. Kennedy was Attorney General 1961–1964 and a New York senator until assassination June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles. Files sit in the RFK collection.
h1: Robert F. Kennedy in the RFK Assassination Records Collection
lede: Robert F. Kennedy served as US Attorney General from 1961–1964 and as a US Senator from New York until his assassination on June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles. Investigative files are central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. BlackVaultDocs’ figure hub matches the name Robert F. Kennedy in document titles from public NARA releases. The hub is a title index, not a biography of the Senate years and not a file count. PDFs remain on the originating archive.

sections.h2: What the RFK figure hub lists
paragraphs: The figure slug robert-f-kennedy groups indexed titles that name Robert F. Kennedy. The packet supplies no document count, so this page does not invent one. The public-record identity in the blurb is: US Attorney General from 1961–1964; US Senator from New York until assassination on June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles; investigative files central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection.

“Central to” is the blurb’s description of where investigative files sit in that collection. It is not a percentage and not a folder count. This overlay does not convert the phrase into a number. A title match is a catalog hit, not a finding that every page of the scan is an investigative report rather than a routine memorandum.

June 5, 1968 and Los Angeles are the date and place the blurb gives for the assassination. 1961–1964 is the Attorney General window. Those bounds are the chronology this page cites. It does not add a hotel name on this packet, because this figure blurb does not name one.

sections.h2: Attorney General years and the 1968 investigative files
paragraphs: The blurb names two public roles before the assassination date: US Attorney General from 1961–1964 and US Senator from New York. Title hits on the hub may reflect either role or the assassination investigation. The packet does not split those classes. This page does not invent that split.

Investigative files are described as central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. Researchers who need the scans should open the originating archive from the figure hub. BlackVaultDocs matches names in titles from public NARA releases; it does not re-host the PDFs.

paragraphs: Figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. The RFK hub is that match, not a complete senatorial archive and not a complete FOIA log. A missing title hit means the indexed title in this ingest did not match the name as implemented.

sections.h2: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: This overlay does not argue who was responsible for the June 5, 1968 assassination in Los Angeles. It restates the packet: Attorney General 1961–1964; Senator from New York until assassination on June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles; investigative files central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. Conspiracy commentary is outside the index.

No NARA ID is in the facts. No document total is in the facts. Cite 1961–1964, June 5, 1968, Los Angeles, and the RFK Assassination Records Collection. Do not attach an invented file count to Kennedy’s name.

The Robert F. Kennedy figure hub is the live title list. All figures shows the rest of the name index. The JFK assassination collection href is the related topic link on this packet. Open the originating archive for scans. A later ingest can retag titles; this prose still will not invent a document count.

The Attorney General window 1961–1964 and the June 5, 1968 assassination in Los Angeles are separate facts in the blurb. Title hits may reflect either public role or the investigative files described as central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. This packet does not split those classes.

faqs.q: How does Robert F. Kennedy appear in the declassified files?
faqs.a: The packet states that he served as US Attorney General from 1961–1964 and as a US Senator from New York until his assassination on June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles. Investigative files are central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. BlackVaultDocs matches the name in indexed titles. This page does not assign a file count.

faqs.q: When and where was Robert F. Kennedy assassinated in this record?
faqs.a: The blurb dates the assassination to June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles. That is the chronology this page cites. The packet does not give a document count for that date. Titles that name Robert F. Kennedy appear on the figure hub; PDFs remain on the originating archive.

faqs.q: Which collection holds investigative files on Robert F. Kennedy?
faqs.a: The blurb says investigative files are central to the RFK Assassination Records Collection. “Central” is not a file count. The packet’s internal topic link is the JFK assassination collection href supplied on the packet. This page does not invent a document total for either label.

faqs.q: Does the RFK figure hub prove a conspiracy?
faqs.a: No. The hub matches the name Robert F. Kennedy in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. It restates the 1961–1964 Attorney General years and the June 5, 1968 assassination in Los Angeles. It does not interpret investigative files as proof of a plot.
